subproblems.title: Integral data of an integer multiplicity representation
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents Z → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ((∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = ∫ x, R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration: this is the exact frozen Lean type of the accepted DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.flat_convergence-a1.localize-a1.imrep_data-a1 (lean_name cmc_fcl_imrep_integral_data), shared here by Lean name; its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim. In the selected proof it supplies step 3(i)-(ii) and step 3(iii) with E = ℝ^P (admissibility of (R.measure, R.orient) and X(ω) = ∫R.orient(ω) dR.measure); it is used by the sibling restrict_im.
Source: facts (R1)-(R4) of the parent proof of cmc_fc_localize, stated for one representation. The parent applies them to IMReps of T_j, of ∂T_j and of T. Parts (a)-(c) and (d) are exactly the hypotheses that (SL) requires of (μ, ξ) and of (μ', ξ').
Notation: ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. By definition (IMRep.measure), R.measure = ν.withDensity(x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞])).
1. (Absolute continuity.) R.measure ≪ ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
2. (a) Let K ⊆ U be compact. K is closed, hence Borel. By withDensity_apply, R.measure(K) = ∫⁻_K θ dν = ∫⁻ θ d(ν⌞K). Since K is measurable, ν⌞K = (μHE[n]⌞M)⌞K = μHE[n]⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). As K ∩ M = M ∩ K, R.measure(K) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ K} θ dHⁿ. This is ≠ ∞ by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult applied to K (K compact, K ⊆ U). Hence R.measure(K) < ∞.
3. (b) The IMRep field aestronglyMeasurable_orient says that ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable. By step 1 and AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac, ξ is R.measure-a.e. strongly measurable.
4. (c) Since R.measure ≪ ν, a property that holds for ν-a.e. x also holds for R.measure-a.e. x (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). Apply this to the property that |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α.
5. (d) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and put F(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. Since R represents Z, Z(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)F(x) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ θ(x)F(x) dν(x).
 The density x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) equals x ↦ ((θ(x) : ℝ≥0) : [0, ∞]) (ENNReal.coe_natCast). The map x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0) is measurable: θ is measurable by the field measurable_mult, composed with the cast ℕ → ℝ≥0 (measurable_from_nat).
 Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul gives ∫ F d(ν.withDensity θ) = ∫ θ(x) • F(x) dν(x). It needs no integrability assumption, since both sides are Bochner integrals. Also θ(x) • F(x) = (θ(x) : ℝ)·F(x) (NNReal.smul_def, NNReal.coe_natCast).
 Hence ∫ F dR.measure = ∫ θF dν = Z(ω). ∎
Appendix (verified Lean). This tactic proof of exactly the frozen statement compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission inside namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
  intro P n U Z R hZ
  have hac : R.measure ≪ μHE[n].restrict R.carrier := withDensity_absolutelyContinuous _ _
  refine ⟨?_, R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient.mono_ac hac, fun h => hac.ae_le h, ?_⟩
  · intro K hK hKU
    have hKm : MeasurableSet K := hK.isClosed.measurableSet
    rw [IMRep.measure, withDensity_apply _ hKm, Measure.restrict_restrict hKm, inter_comm]
    exact lt_top_iff_ne_top.2 (R.locallyIntegrable_mult K hK hKU)
  · intro ω
    rw [hZ ω, IMRep.action, IMRep.measure]
    have hf : Measurable fun x => (R.mult x : NNReal) := by
      exact (measurable_from_nat (f := fun k : ℕ => (k : NNReal))).comp R.measurable_mult
    have hcoe : (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞)) = fun x => (((R.mult x : NNReal)) : ℝ≥0∞) := by
      funext x; simp
    rw [hcoe, integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul hf]
    congr 1
proof_key_steps: R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M.
Finite on compacts: withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict reduce R.measure(K) to ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult).
a.e. strong measurability of ξ and the a.e. unit bound transfer from Hⁿ⌞M to R.measure by absolute continuity.
Z(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫⟨ω,ξ⟩ dR.measure by integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul.

subproblems.title: Measure and action of the Borel restriction of an integer multiplicity representation
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) and R' be IMReps in U (IMRep U n), let A ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and let E ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set. Assume R' represents A, carrier(R') = M ∩ E, mult(R') = θ and orient(R') = ξ. Then R'.measure = R.measure⌞E (the restriction R.measure.restrict E), and A(ω) = ∫_E ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dR.measure(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = ξ(x)(ω(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R R' : IMRep U n) (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet E → R'.Represents A → R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E → R'.mult = R.mult → R'.orient = R.orient → R'.measure = R.measure.restrict E ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, A ω = ∫ x in E, R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂R.measure

1. (Measures.) By definition (IMRep.measure), R.measure = (ν⌞M).withDensity θ. Using carrier(R') = M ∩ E and mult(R') = θ, R'.measure = (ν⌞(M ∩ E)).withDensity θ.
2. E is Borel, so Mathlib restrict_withDensity gives R.measure⌞E = ((ν⌞M).withDensity θ)⌞E = ((ν⌞M)⌞E).withDensity θ. Measure.restrict_restrict (E measurable) gives (ν⌞M)⌞E = ν⌞(E ∩ M) = ν⌞(M ∩ E). Comparing with step 1, R'.measure = R.measure⌞E.

This gives A(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) d(R.measure⌞E)(x) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x); the last equality is the definition of the set integral. ∎

subproblems.title: Mass of a current given by integration against a measure with unit-bounded orientation
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and X ∈ 𝒟_d(U). Let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P, let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_d(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P d), and let E, V ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets. Assume that for μ-a.e. x, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every d-covector α (|α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α, ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = ξ(x)(α)). Assume also that X(ω) = ∫_E ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dμ(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U). Then M_V(X) = X.massOn V ≤ μ(E ∩ V).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U d) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P d) (E V : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) d, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U d, X ω = ∫ x in E, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ) → X.massOn V ≤ μ (E ∩ V)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration: this is the exact frozen Lean type of the accepted DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.flat_convergence-a1.localize-a1.mass_le_measure-a1 (lean_name cmc_fcl_massOn_le_measure_inter), shared here by Lean name; its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim. In the selected proof it supplies step 6(i): with X := B_t, (μ, ξ) := (μ', ξ'), E := {f < t} and V := W it gives M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'({f < t} ∩ W) ≤ μ'(closure W) < ∞.
Source: the mass estimates of steps 0 and 8 of the parent proof of cmc_fc_localize. These rest on (R3): if |ω| ≤ 1, then ∫_B⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ ≤ μ(B). Here the estimate is stated for an arbitrary integral current and an arbitrary region V. The parent uses it with X = A_{φ(j)}(s), E = {g < s}, V = U (M(T'_j) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}({g < s})), with X = B_{φ(j)}(s) (M(B) ≤ μ'_{φ(j)}({g < s})), and with μ = 0 for the zero current in step 0. The integral is the Bochner integral, which is 0 for non-integrable integrands, so no finiteness or integrability assumption is needed.
1. By definition, M_V(X) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) over the admissible ω: those ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U d V). Fix such an ω. It suffices (sSup_le) to show ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ μ(E ∩ V).
2. Put f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) and S := tsupport ω, a closed (hence Borel) set with S ⊆ V. Then ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) = ENNReal.ofReal(∫_E f dμ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal|∫_E f dμ| = ‖∫_E f dμ‖ₑ (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs) ≤ ∫⁻_E ‖f‖ₑ dμ. The last inequality is Mathlib enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, which holds for every f.
3. Claim: ‖f(x)‖ₑ ≤ 1_S(x) for μ⌞E-a.e. x. The hypothesis holds μ-a.e., hence μ⌞E-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae). If x ∈ S, then ‖f(x)‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal|ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal|ω(x)| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal 1 = 1, by the hypothesis with α := ω(x) and by admissibility. If x ∉ S, then ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so f(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0.
4. By lintegral_mono_ae, ∫⁻_E ‖f‖ₑ dμ ≤ ∫⁻_E 1_S dμ = (μ⌞E)(S) = μ(S ∩ E), using lintegral_indicator_one and Measure.restrict_apply (S Borel). Since S ⊆ V, μ(S ∩ E) ≤ μ(E ∩ V) (measure_mono).
5. Combining steps 2-4, ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ μ(E ∩ V) for every admissible ω. Hence M_V(X) ≤ μ(E ∩ V). ∎
Appendix (verified Lean). This tactic proof of exactly the frozen statement compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission inside namespace GMT.Ch07 with the contract's opens. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
  intro P d U X μ ξ E V hξ hX
  apply sSup_le
  rintro r ⟨ω, hω, rfl⟩
  show ENNReal.ofReal (X ω) ≤ _
  rw [hX ω]
  have hS : MeasurableSet (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)) :=
    (isClosed_tsupport _).measurableSet
  calc ENNReal.ofReal (∫ x in E, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ)
        ≤ ‖∫ x in E, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ‖ₑ := by
        rw [Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs]
        exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (le_abs_self _)
    _ ≤ ∫⁻ x in E, ‖ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x)‖ₑ ∂μ :=
        enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm _
    _ ≤ ∫⁻ x in E, (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)).indicator 1 x ∂μ := by
        apply lintegral_mono_ae
        filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae hξ] with x hx
        by_cases hxs : x ∈ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)
        · rw [indicator_of_mem hxs, Pi.one_apply, Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs]
          calc ENNReal.ofReal |ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x)|
              ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x)) :=
                ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (hx _)
            _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal 1 := ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal (hω.2 x)

        · rw [indicator_of_notMem hxs]
          have h0 : (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x = 0 := image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hxs
          simp [h0]
    _ = μ.restrict E (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d)) := lintegral_indicator_one hS
    _ = μ (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) ∩ E) := Measure.restrict_apply hS

a.e. on E, ‖⟨ω,ξ⟩‖ₑ ≤ 1_{tsupport ω}: the unit bound and |ω| ≤ 1 hold on the support, and ω = 0 off it.

subproblems.title: Borel restrictions of admissible representations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity
subproblems.statement: Assume (IMC)(b): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every IMRep R in U of degree n and every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R'.Represents A, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult and R'.orient = R.orient. Assume (IMC)(d): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P and every IMRep R in U of degree n, for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) one has |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Assume (RU), the frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq: for all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, all measures μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ on ℝ^P that are finite on every compact subset of U and all fields ξ₁, ξ₂, ξ₃ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) such that each ξ_i is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable and satisfies |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ_i-a.e. x and every k-covector α, if ∫ ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫ ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫ ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), then ∫_B ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_B ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫_B ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃ for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let P, q ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let X, A ∈ 𝒟_q(U) with X integer multiplicity. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_q(ℝ^P) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and every q-covector α, such that X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U). Let E ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set with A(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U) (Bochner integrals). Then A is integer multiplicity.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the supplied proof of cbr_cc_slice_property_of_im (the proofs that A_t and B_t are integer multiplicity), isolated for an arbitrary integer multiplicity X ∈ 𝒟_q(U), an arbitrary admissible representation (μ, ξ) of X and an arbitrary Borel set E. The parent applies it twice with U := ℝ^P and E := {f < t}: with (q, X, μ, ξ, A) := (d + 1, X, μ, ξ, A_t) and with (q, X, μ, ξ, A) := (d, ∂X, μ', ξ', B_t). Step 3 of the supplied proof is provided by the reused siblings imrep_data (cmc_fcl_imrep_integral_data) and imrep_restrict (cmc_fcl_imrep_restrict_formula).
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for a field ζ and a form ω, ζ(ω) denotes the function x ↦ ζ(x)(ω(x)); H^q := μHE[q].
1. (Representation of X.) Since X is integer multiplicity, there is an IMRep R_X = (M, θ, ζ) in U of degree q with R_X.Represents X. Put ν := R_X.measure = (H^q⌞M).withDensity θ.
2. (Restricted IMRep.) U is open and E is Borel, so (IMC)(b) applied to R_X and E gives a current A' ∈ 𝒟_q(U) and an IMRep R' in U with R'.Represents A', R'.carrier = M ∩ E, R'.mult = θ and R'.orient = ζ.
3. (Admissibility of (ν, ζ).) The sibling imrep_data applied to the current X and its representation R_X gives: (a) ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (b) ζ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) if |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α for H^q⌞M-a.e. x, then the same holds for ν-a.e. x; (d) X(ω) = ∫ ζ(ω) dν for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U). The hypothesis of (c) is exactly (IMC)(d) for R_X, so |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α holds for ν-a.e. x.
4. (Applying (RU).) Apply (RU) with k := q, the open set U, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (ν, ζ) and (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0), the zero measure with the zero field x ↦ 0. Its hypotheses hold. Finiteness on compact subsets of U: for μ by assumption, for ν by 3(a), and trivially for the zero measure. A.e. strong measurability: for ξ by assumption, for ζ by 3(b), and for the constant field 0 because constant functions are strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_const). Unit bounds: for ξ by assumption, for ζ by step 3, and for the zero measure because every property holds a.e. for it (its a.e. filter is ⊥). The identity: for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U), ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω) = ∫ ζ(ω) dν = ∫ ζ(ω) dν + ∫ 0 d0, by the representation hypothesis on (μ, ξ), by 3(d), and because every integral against the zero measure is 0 (integral_zero_measure). The conclusion of (RU) with the Borel set B := E gives, for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U), ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν + ∫_E 0 d0 = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν, because the restriction of the zero measure is the zero measure (Measure.restrict_zero) and its integral vanishes.
5. (Applying imrep_restrict.) The sibling imrep_restrict applied to R := R_X, R', A' and E (E Borel, R' represents A', carrier(R') = M ∩ E, mult(R') = θ, orient(R') = ζ) gives A'(ω) = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν for every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U).
6. (Conclusion.) For every ω ∈ 𝒟^q(U), A(ω) = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ (hypothesis on A) = ∫_E ζ(ω) dν (step 4) = A'(ω) (step 5) = R'.action(ω) (R' represents A'). Hence R'.Represents A, so A is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity A is witnessed by R'). ∎

subproblems.title: Almost every slice defect has finite mass on bounded sets
subproblems.statement: Assume (MM), the third conjunct of the frozen statement of the sibling cbr_measure_convergence_tools: for every P ∈ ℕ, all measures μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) on ℝ^P, every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, every G ⊆ ℝ^P, all a, b ∈ ℝ, every L ∈ ℝ≥0 and all Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] (j ∈ ℕ) with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for every j and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹·μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every j and every t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_{j→∞} Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dt ≤ L·liminf_{j→∞} μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P, q ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, Z : ℝ → 𝒟_q(U) (t ↦ Z_t), a measure μ on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, a continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ and L ∈ ℝ≥0, and assume M_W(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P and every t ∈ ℝ. Here M_W(T) := T.massOn W, h⁻¹ is read as ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹, and the liminf is taken along 𝓝[>] 0 in [0, ∞]. Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ one has M_W(Z_t) < ∞ for every bounded W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ j, μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) < ∞) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → Z j t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs j (G ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => Z j t) atTop ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun j => μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})) atTop) → ∀ (P q : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Z : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U q) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), Continuous f → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (t : ℝ), IsOpen W → (Z t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), Bornology.IsBounded W → (Z t).massOn W < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cbr_cc_slice_property_of_im, isolated for an arbitrary family Z of currents with the liminf mass bound. The parent applies it with U := ℝ^P, q := d, Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t and the bound supplied by (SL); f is continuous because it is Lipschitz.
Notation: M_W(T) := T.massOn W; B_k := ball(0, k) (open) and B̄_k := closedBall(0, k) for k ∈ ℕ; volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ.
1. (Setup.) Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and put G := B_k, a := −m, b := m. Since G ∩ {a < f < b} ⊆ B_k ⊆ B̄_k and B̄_k is compact (isCompact_closedBall; ℝ^P is proper), μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}) ≤ μ(B̄_k) < ∞ (measure_mono and the hypothesis on μ).
2. (Applying (MM).) Apply (MM) with P, the constant sequence μ_j := μ (j ∈ ℕ), f, G, a, b, L and the constant sequence Z_j(t) := M_{B_k}(Z_t) (j ∈ ℕ, t ∈ ℝ). Its hypotheses hold: f is continuous; μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for every j by step 1; and for every j and every t ∈ (a, b), Z_j(t) = M_{B_k}(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} h⁻¹·μ(B_k ∩ {t − h < f < t}) by the hypothesis on Z applied to the open set W := B_k (isOpen_ball). (MM) yields a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with (i) liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t such that t ∈ (a, b), and (ii) ∫_{(a,b)} g dt ≤ L·liminf_j μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}).
3. (Constant sequences.) The filter atTop on ℕ is nontrivial, so the liminf of a constant sequence equals its value (Filter.liminf_const). Thus (i) says: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies M_{B_k}(Z_t) ≤ g(t); and (ii) says ∫_{(−m,m)} g dt ≤ L·μ(B_k ∩ {−m < f < m}), which is < ∞ because (L : [0, ∞]) < ∞ and by step 1 (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
4. (Finiteness of g.) g is measurable and its integral with respect to volume⌞(−m, m) is finite, so g(t) < ∞ for volume⌞(−m, m)-a.e. t (ae_lt_top). Since (−m, m) is measurable, this means: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies g(t) < ∞ (ae_restrict_iff'). Intersecting with step 3: for a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies M_{B_k}(Z_t) ≤ g(t) < ∞.
5. (Countable intersection.) ℕ is countable, so by ae_all_iff, applied over k and then over m, there is one Lebesgue-null set N such that for every t ∉ N and all k, m ∈ ℕ: t ∈ (−m, m) implies M_{B_k}(Z_t) < ∞.
6. (Conclusion.) Let t ∉ N and let W ⊆ ℝ^P be bounded. Then W ⊆ ball(0, r) for some r ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). Choose k ∈ ℕ with r < k (exists_nat_gt), so W ⊆ B_k (ball_subset_ball). Choose m ∈ ℕ with |t| < m, so −m < t < m. By monotonicity of the local mass in the region (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono) and step 5, M_W(Z_t) ≤ M_{B_k}(Z_t) < ∞. Since N is null, for L¹-a.e. t this holds for every bounded W. ∎
